components.name: Let Milo Play Button
components.description: The primary handoff control; leaf green at rest and vermilion while Milo is running.
components.css: .ds-btn-milo { min-height:46px; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; padding:11px 17px; border:2px solid var(--ink, #20261f); border-radius:12px 14px 11px 15px; color:var(--paper-light, #fff8e8); background-color:var(--green, #5b9b5a); font:900 15px/1 'Nunito Sans', sans-serif; box-shadow:3px 7px 18px rgba(32,38,31,.16); transform:rotate(-1deg); transition:transform .18s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), box-shadow .18s ease; cursor:pointer; } .ds-btn-milo-dot { width:10px; height:10px; border:2px solid currentColor; border-radius:50%; background:var(--yellow, #f4b93a); } .ds-btn-milo:hover { transform:translateY(-3px) rotate(0); box-shadow:4px 10px 22px rgba(32,38,31,.2); } .ds-btn-milo:active { transform:translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-milo:focus-visible { outline:4px solid var(--blue, #3367b1); outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Mix a New Board Button
components.description: The sunny reset action, styled as a slightly skewed painted tab.
components.css: .ds-btn-new { min-height:46px; padding:11px 17px; border:2px solid var(--ink, #20261f); border-radius:12px 14px 11px 15px; color:var(--ink, #20261f); background:var(--yellow, #f4b93a); font:900 15px/1 'Nunito Sans', sans-serif; box-shadow:3px 7px 18px rgba(32,38,31,.16); transform:rotate(1deg); transition:transform .18s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), box-shadow .18s ease; cursor:pointer; } .ds-btn-new:hover { transform:translateY(-3px) rotate(0); box-shadow:4px 10px 22px rgba(32,38,31,.2); } .ds-btn-new:active { transform:translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-new:focus-visible { outline:4px solid var(--blue, #3367b1); outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Secondary Paper Button
components.description: A quieter outlined action used inside game-result overlays.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height:46px; padding:11px 17px; border:2px solid var(--ink, #20261f); border-radius:12px 14px 11px 15px; color:var(--ink, #20261f); background:var(--paper-light, #fff8e8); font:900 15px/1 'Nunito Sans', sans-serif; box-shadow:3px 7px 18px rgba(32,38,31,.16); transition:transform .18s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), box-shadow .18s ease; cursor:pointer; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { transform:translateY(-3px); box-shadow:4px 10px 22px rgba(32,38,31,.2); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform:translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline:4px solid var(--blue, #3367b1); outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Score Card
components.description: A compact ink plaque with a tracked label and tabular display numeral.
components.css: .ds-score { min-width:88px; padding:10px 14px 9px; border:2px solid var(--ink, #20261f); border-radius:12px 14px 10px 15px; color:var(--paper-light, #fff8e8); background:var(--ink, #20261f); text-align:center; box-shadow:3px 6px 16px rgba(32,38,31,.18); } .ds-score span { display:block; color:#e8dec5; font:900 9px/1 'Nunito Sans', sans-serif; letter-spacing:.12em; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-score strong { display:block; margin-top:1px; font:400 19px/1.1 'Bowlby One', sans-serif; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; }

components.name: Painted Number Tile
components.description: The core painted-lot primitive, pairing value text with a stable color progression.
components.css: .ds-tile { width:132px; aspect-ratio:1; display:grid; place-items:center; border:2px solid var(--ink, #20261f); border-radius:10px 15px 11px 14px; color:var(--paper-light, #fff8e8); background:#8a5ba1; font:400 42px/1 'Bowlby One', sans-serif; letter-spacing:-.025em; box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 2px rgba(255,248,232,.2); transform:rotate(-.6deg); transition:transform .18s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); } .ds-tile:hover { transform:translateY(-2px) rotate(0); } .ds-tile:focus-visible { outline:4px solid var(--blue, #3367b1); outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Milo Decision Mark
components.description: The signature companion readout: a painted directional mark paired with explicit move and timing text.
components.html: Last move — Moved right18.4 ms
components.css: .ds-decision { display:grid; grid-template-columns:100px 1fr; align-items:center; gap:24px; color:var(--ink, #20261f); font-family:'Nunito Sans', sans-serif; } .ds-direction { width:100px; height:100px; display:grid; place-items:center; border:3px solid var(--ink, #20261f); border-radius:49% 51% 43% 57%; background:var(--yellow, #f4b93a); box-shadow:5px 10px 20px rgba(32,38,31,.16); transform:rotate(-4deg); transition:transform .18s cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); } .ds-direction svg { width:53px; height:53px; fill:none; stroke:currentColor; stroke-width:2.4; stroke-linecap:round; stroke-linejoin:round; } .ds-decision:hover .ds-direction { transform:translateY(-3px) rotate(-2deg); } .ds-decision strong { display:block; font:400 24px/1.05 'Bowlby One', sans-serif; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-decision div > span { display:block; margin-top:4px; color:var(--red, #e9573f); font-weight:900; }

narrative.overview:
The 2048 board is a painted little town that Milo learns to navigate. Broad gouache fields, warm paper, fine ink outlines, and deliberately imperfect geometry make the game feel assembled by hand while clear labels and stable placement keep every action immediately operable.

This world is colorful, companionable, tactile, and gently mischievous. Expression comes from pigment, irregular silhouettes, small rotations, and stateful motion—not from ornamental dashboard chrome. It explicitly refuses the beige utility-dashboard language common to puzzle and AI interfaces.
keyCharacteristics: Warm parchment beneath decisive vermilion, cobalt, marigold, leaf, and lilac fields.
Fine near-black outlines that keep painted surfaces legible and operational.
Chunky display numerals paired with friendly, high-weight utility text.
Slightly skewed controls and asymmetric corners, always within a stable layout.
Milo presented as a companion inside the same game world, not as a detached analytics panel.

rules.name: The Painted Field Rule
rules.body: Saturated colors appear as broad, bounded fields with ink edges; do not scatter them as tiny dashboard-status accents.

rules.name: The Cobalt Focus Rule
rules.body: Every interactive control uses the same unmistakable cobalt focus outline, regardless of its resting paint color.

rules.name: The Chunk and Whisper Rule
rules.body: Use Bowlby One for the few facts that should feel monumental; let Nunito Sans carry all explanation and operation.

rules.name: The Shared-Board Rule
rules.body: Scores, controls, board, and Milo describe one live session; never separate Milo into a remote dashboard or a competing page region.

rules.name: The Paper, Not Glass Rule
rules.body: Shadows imply layered card and painted board stock; never use blur-heavy glass panels, glossy reflections, or floating SaaS cards.

rules.name: The Gentle Skew Rule
rules.body: Rotation adds handmade character to a control or focal object, but must reset or settle on interaction and must never disturb alignment or hit areas.

dos: Do keep the board the largest object and Milo the clear second focal point.
Do use broad gouache fields, fine ink outlines, uneven radii, and small rotations as one coherent material language.
Do preserve semantic controls, visible cobalt focus states, direct keyboard and touch input, and non-color state labels.
Do keep generated raster texture content-free and preserve embedded provenance on every shipping raster.
Do place the complete board before Milo on mobile, with the studio following immediately below.
donts: Don't turn the experience into a beige utility dashboard, analytics console, or grid of interchangeable rounded cards.
Don't use color alone to communicate Milo's state, the latest move, tile value, or game outcome.
Don't add glassmorphism, glossy gradients, generic icon-library ornament, or perfect corporate geometry.
Don't let texture compete with tile numerals, control labels, or telemetry.
Don't expand the palette casually; the compact paint box is part of the identity.
